key_insight: Human and LLM-generated synthesis recipes achieved comparable lab success, and their closed-loop collaboration helped discover a new materials prototype, Ba3PtO5.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that AI can accelerate experimental materials synthesis by proposing viable reaction pathways, especially when paired with human oversight and feedback from laboratory validation.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper-related materials using both humans and LLMs.
Tested recipe outcomes through in-lab experiments and fed results back into a closed-loop collaboration.
Compared performance across two rounds to assess how human and LLM suggestions improve with feedback.
evidence_signal: Measured success rates were similar for humans and LLMs on known materials (83% vs 75% in round one; 79% vs 71% in round two) but much lower for unknown targets, and the collaboration enabled discovery of Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Results are based on a specific materials family, so performance may not transfer directly to other chemistries or more complex synthesis spaces.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
